note: Adjudicated accidental variants (punctuation). Substantive text agrees across both witnesses with zero variants.

adjudicated.ruling: Full stop after Orémus, with handmissal-eo. DO's comma is a consequence of its layout: the parenthetical rubric follows on the same line, so the invitation is left open. Here the rubric stands as its own segment and the invitation is a complete utterance — the only words of this prayer said aloud.
The page sets Orémus inside the rubric that runs on, with a comma. The edition prints it as its own line, with a full stop.

No comma before the apposition Dóminum, with handmissal-eo and with the corpus rulings at ordinarium.confiteor w064 and ordinarium.sanctus w004: Christum Dóminum nostrum is one unbroken title, and this is the standard closing formula of a collect.

No comma before the 'et' joining the second genitive, with handmissal-eo: mérita governs both genitives — the merits of the saints whose relics are here and of all the saints — so the two depend on the same noun and are not separated.
